# datadog_incident_handle (Resource)

Provides a Datadog global incident handle resource. An incident handle (for example `@incident-sev-1`) can be mentioned in monitor notifications to declare an incident with the configured incident type and fields. Note: the Datadog API has no endpoint to delete a single handle, so destroying this resource only removes it from Terraform state; delete the handle in the Datadog UI.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "datadog_incident_type" "critical" {
  name        = "Critical"
  description = "Customer-impacting incidents"
}

# Mentioning @incident-p1 in a monitor notification declares a SEV-1 Critical incident.
resource "datadog_incident_handle" "p1" {
  name             = "@incident-p1"
  incident_type_id = datadog_incident_type.critical.id
  severity         = ["SEV-1"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `incident_type_id` (String) The ID of the incident type for incidents declared through this handle.
- `name` (String) The handle name, including the leading `@`, for example `@incident-sev-1`.

### Optional

- `commander_user_id` (String) The ID of the user assigned as incident commander for incidents declared through this handle.
- `severity` (List of String) Severities set on incidents declared through this handle, for example `["SEV-1"]`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the incident handle.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import datadog_incident_handle.p1 "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
```
